The poem is a double sestina whose end-word sequence (mountains/valleys/forests/music/morning/evening and their prescribed rotations) is rigidly fixed. All 72 lines plus the envoi already obey that sequence exactly, so the only disruption that can exist is a content swap between two lines whose end-words happen to be identical (so the surface pattern still looks intact).

Lines 25 and 32 both end on the required word “music.” Swapping them restores two local anomalies that the sestina form itself cannot tolerate:

- Line 25 (“These forests eke, made wretched by our music”) now belongs to Klaius, who has just been speaking of “we”/“our”; the plural possessive is therefore appropriate.  
- Line 32 (“Have prayed me leave my strange exclaiming music”) now belongs to Strephon, whose entire stanza is in the first-person singular; the singular “my” is therefore appropriate.

No other pair of identically-ending lines produces a comparable restoration of both grammar and dramatic voice. Hence the two lines that were transposed are 25 and 32.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: 25 and 32
